_meta.purpose: Track per-skill quality scores across invocations

scoring_rubric.10: Flawless — perfect execution, exceeded expectations, zero rework
scoring_rubric.9: Excellent — all success criteria met, minimal polish
scoring_rubric.8: Strong — correct execution, minor adjustments only
scoring_rubric.7: Good — correct, one small correction needed

_meta.update_instructions:
Append to runs[] after each non-trivial invocation. Recompute average_score. Update last_updated.

Run entry schema:
{
  "run_id": "<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>-<6hex>",
  "session_id": "<env:CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID or 'unknown'>",
  "timestamp": "<ISO-8601>",
  "invocation_trigger": "claude-proactive",
  "arguments": "<args string>",
  "score": null,
  "outcome": null,
  "duration_ms": <int>,
  "trace": {
    "output_length_tokens": null,
    "tool_calls_made": [],
    "final_lines": "<last 300 chars of output>",
    "failure_reason": null
  },
  "human_review": {
    "scored_at": null,
    "correction": null,
    "note": null
  }
}

Score with: /score-skill --skill <name>  |  Optimize: /optimize-skill --skill <name> (needs 10+ scored runs)

criteria.stack_coverage: Does it generate trees for all requested stack components (Airflow, dbt, PySpark)?
criteria.depth_level: Does minimal/standard/full produce correctly scoped output without over- or under-generating?
criteria.naming_conventions: Does output follow all naming patterns — DAG filenames (snake_case), dbt models (layer__entity), Python packages (__init__.py present)?
criteria.generator_only: Does it output file trees and stubs without executing any shell commands, dbt runs, or Airflow triggers?
criteria.file_stub_accuracy: Are pyproject.toml, dbt_project.yml, and DAG stubs syntactically correct and immediately usable?
criteria.anti_pattern_avoidance: Does it flag or avoid known data engineering anti-patterns (top-level DAG code, hardcoded credentials, missing tests dir)?

description: GENERATOR — scaffolds mature folder/boilerplate structure for Airflow 3.1.7 + dbt + PySpark data projects. Evaluates: stack coverage, depth-level correctness, naming convention enforcement, GENERATOR-only constraint adherence, file stub accuracy.
